comment: The section allows an element to be realised centrally, federatively, or distributively, but it does not define the minimum behaviours that must remain consistent across those topologies.

anchor.note: p.47 l.Lines 127-131 read as the printed page; section 3.2 agrees

public.text: The section allows an element to be realised centrally, federatively, or distributively, but it does not define the minimum behaviours that must remain consistent across those topologies.
public.suggestedRevision: For every component, define topology-independent requirements covering authoritative responsibility, interfaces, identifiers, data consistency, discovery, access control, audit, conformance, availability, and lifecycle management.
